name: Flock Safety

summary.text: Flock Safety is an Atlanta-based maker of automated licence-plate-reader cameras and related surveillance software sold to police departments, municipalities and private customers. In March 2025 Andreessen Horowitz led a funding round of about $275 million that valued the company at roughly $7.5 billion; the company says it serves more than 5,000 law-enforcement agencies. In 2025–2026 a number of U.S. cities ended or paused Flock contracts over privacy concerns and fears the data could be used for federal immigration enforcement.

facts.claim: In March 2025 Bloomberg reported that Andreessen Horowitz was set to lead a funding round of about $250 million valuing Flock Safety at roughly $7.5 billion; Axios later reported the round closed at $275 million at that valuation.

facts.claim: TechSpot counted 38 U.S. cities that rejected or switched off Flock cameras over a six-month period, mainly citing privacy concerns and fears of federal immigration use; Flock says many cities have since signed new contracts.

facts.claim: In April 2026 a secondary share sale reportedly valued Flock at close to $8.4 billion.

openQuestions: Sources disagree on the date of the $7.5 billion round (March vs September 2025) and on the community count (5,000 agencies vs 5,000–6,000 communities). Specific municipal contracts were not retrieved; the owner may wish to cite individual city council records.
